description: By day, Arcana is an urban greenhouse and plant store, and by night, it becomes a natural wine bar and live music venue. Hosting live bands, DJs, and club nights, Arcana’s genres range from house to R&B to jazz. Founder Naz Khorram’s vision was to create a feeling of ““being drawn into space without necessarily defining what we are about.”

name: The Faight
description: The Faight is an art and performance space in the Lower Height hosting DIY and experimental shows. It was founded in 2023 to revive the arts in San Francisco post-pandemic and support the local community through workshops, events, and pop-ups. Co-owner Daniel Bondi explained in 2026 that they are working to start a nonprofit to get grants and additional funding to run The Faight. He explains, “We are first and foremost a community space,” he said. “Our whole mission is to give artists and musicians a platform to grow.”

name: Music City Starfactory
description:
Music City Starfactory, formerly Music City San Francisco, opened as a nonprofit 29,000-square-foot music complex in 2024. It was originally conceptualized when founder Rudy Colombini bought the building in 1988 for $4 million and opened Music City San in 2005. In 2024, a major $20 million renovation was completed and the organization was rebranded to Music City Starfactory. The new site had 20 rehearsal rooms, performance spaces, a bar and restaurant, and a hotel. Colombini wanted to create an entire music ecosystem in one building where artists could rehearse, perform, and stay with the goal of supporting small local artists. Other initiatives include growing the San Francisco Music Hall of Fame, which is housed in the Music City Starfactory and preserves local music history, booking commission-free gigs for local artists, and providing educational scholarships. The organization and investment aimed to revive San Francisco as a musical city comparable to Los Angeles or New York; a place where musicians stay to grow their careers. Colombini said in 2023, “This is the seed that will make San Francisco into another star of a city for music, which hasn’t been for 25 years” 

Shortly after the grand opening though, Music City defaulted on a $10 million construction loan and was behind three months of rent payments, about $76,000 per month. The financial margins of the venue are complicated: since the aim is to be affordable to local artists, it only costs $50 for a two-hour recording session. In response to this, Colombini says to SFGate, “I’m kind of nuts,” describing the organization as “one big philanthropy project.” The future of Music City is uncertain with Colombini looking for new revenue streams such as  reality TV, residencies, or streaming infrastructure.

name: Stookey's Blue Room
owner: Tim Stookey, Leslie Cole Stookey, and Aaron Cole
description: Right next to Stookey’s Club Moderne sits Stookey’s Blue Room, sister bars in the Lower Nob Hill neighborhood. While Moderne is a ‘30s and ‘40s inspired cocktail lounge, the Blue Room focuses more on late 20th century live music, jazz, and cabaret shows.

name: Atelier Kromatica
owner: Tin Yi Chelsea Wong, a pianist and San Francisco Conservatory of Music alumna.
description: Atelier Kromatica is an experimental art house focused on reimagining classical music. The artistic director, pianist Tin Yi Chelsea Wong, is known for projects including “Piano at the Palace” and “Piano Beach Bonfire Series” where she and Atelier Kromatica bring free, outdoor piano performances to the Palace of Fine Arts and Ocean Beach. Atelier Kromatica vision is multidisciplinary, blending tech, sculpture, and theater with live piano performances.

name: Sunset Village Music Hall
owner: Thomas Kerbleski through Relax Harder LLC
description: Housed inside a former church, the Sunset Village Music Hall is only temporary. The church was bought for $3.15 million to be turned into a seven story, 45-unit apartment building, but until then it’s a music venue. Local musician and surfer Sam Fickinger is the booking manager, and he says the venue, while likely only to be there for three or four years, is filling a gap in the Outer Sunset: “Everyone’s been looking for a place to play… We more than ever need a space to gather that’s not in our homes.”

name: Club Darc
description: Created by California concert promoter Goldenvoice in collaboration with the business arm of the San Francisco Giants, Club Darc is an warehouse-style EDM, electronic, and techno venue. Danny Bell, Club Darc founder said in a statement, “our goal is to further the mission of making San Francisco a global hub for electronic music.”
